title: Tiredness
whatItIs: Tiredness slows your reactions and can make you fall asleep at the wheel for a few seconds without knowing it.
keyFacts: Plan a break of at least 15 minutes after every 2 hours of driving.
Avoid long journeys between midnight and 6 am, when you are naturally least alert.
If you feel sleepy, stop somewhere safe as soon as you can. Not on a motorway hard shoulder.
The best fixes: two cups of caffeinated coffee and a short nap of at least 15 minutes.
Keep fresh air flowing in the car, but don't rely on an open window to keep you awake.

onTheTest.question: You feel sleepy while driving on a motorway. What should you do?
options: Leave at the next exit and stop somewhere safe
Stop on the hard shoulder for a nap
Open the window and keep going
onTheTest.why: Leave the motorway and stop in a safe place to rest. The hard shoulder is for emergencies only.

traps: The hard shoulder is not a place to rest.
Fresh air and loud music only hide tiredness for a short time.
Long night journeys are riskiest between midnight and 6 am.
